about.title: About the System
about.description: A system to help manage badminton tournaments, register players, and track match results easily.
about.objective1: Create a website to help manage tournament data, reducing redundant paperwork traditionally done in Excel.
about.objective2: Provide an automated matchmaking and bracketing system for both singles and doubles to standardize competitions.
about.objective3: Keep match history records to be used for player ranking and easier decision-making.
about.objective4: Allow players to view schedules and tournament information online instantly, adding convenience and speed.
about.benefit2: Reduce workflow steps and simplify complex data storage compared to Excel.
about.benefit3: Calculate costs easily with a shuttlecock pricing system.
about.benefit4: Systematic reporting of tournament results, increasing transparency and reliability.

defaultRules: - The times specified in the schedule are estimates only. If the competition runs faster than scheduled, the team may call athletes to compete earlier, but not earlier than the registration period. Therefore, athletes must report no later than the specified time to prevent disqualification.

- The team will primarily call athletes based on the 'match order'. Please be prepared. Once announced onto the court, if the athlete does not appear within 5 minutes or arrives unprepared (e.g., hasn't changed clothes, worn shoes, or requested a restroom break), the team will announce again and start a 5-minute timer. If still not ready after the second timer, the ready opponent will win by Bye.

- Athletes must participate in at least 1 match in the group stage (excluding Bye matches) to be eligible for the Lower Knock Out Bracket (if any). If not playing at all in the group stage, the team reserves the right to disqualify the athlete from the Knock Out round.

- If an athlete arrives at the court but refuses to compete or intentionally defaults, it will be considered cheating upon detection. The team has the right to default all remaining matches immediately.

- The competition schedule may run faster or slower than announced. The team will primarily follow the 'match order'. Please remember your match number in both group and Knock Out stages to be prepared when your match approaches.
- Athletes competing in more than 1 category in the group stage must compete consecutively. For Knock Out rounds, there will be a 5-10 minute break before the next match.

- After a match, athletes must record the score on the score sheet, verify its accuracy, and sign it. Then, return the score sheet with the racket and pen to the operating table. Once received, the result is final and cannot be modified (except in cases of actual scoring errors).

- Athletes can check scores via the online system at all times. If you find a score error, please notify the team immediately before the Knock Out bracket is announced. Changes cannot be made once the bracket is published.
- The online system provides a page to check active matches and courts. In case you miss the audio announcement or need to step away, check the system to prevent a Bye.

- Scoring in the Knock Out round for some categories may have different rules. After completing all group stage matches, please check your scores before leaving. If you leave and are called to compete again, failure to appear within the specified time will be considered a forfeit, and the opponent will win by Bye without dispute.

- If an athlete gets injured, up to 2 medical timeouts per match are allowed, totaling no more than 10 minutes. If the athlete cannot return after the time elapses or gets re-injured upon returning, the match will be terminated, and the opponent will win by Bye for the athlete's safety.
- During a match, reaching 11 points allows a 60-second break, and a 120-second break follows the end of each game.
